headline: Cross-family consolidation pass across all 6 B0-B6 candidate families (~11k rows, 14 JSONL files): found and FIXED two real, verified bugs (not just reported), confirmed the other 12 files reproduce byte-identically from source, chatgpt-secondary review was sent but could not be harvested before the browser daemon crashed mid-session.
state: Gabriel's instruction: review the complete B0-B6 candidate dataset with chatgpt-secondary as independent reviewer, verify any findings independently (as done for the earlier B1 0.276-bit case), fix what's real, report honestly. Self-review first (before consulting chatgpt-secondary), across all 14 committed JSONL files in research_entity/claycode/training/ (22188 total lines including the expected B1-full-pool/B1-balanced-subset overlap): 0 JSON parse errors; training_eligible and canonical_truth_allowed correctly false on every single row; 0 cross-family duplicate-prompt CONTRADICTIONS (4464 prompt overlaps found are exactly the B1-full-pool vs B1-balanced-2order-subset relationship, identical target both times, not a bug). Two real, fixable issues found and FIXED this pass (both committed in 82a6568, pushed as 2092e6b): (1) field-naming inconsistency -- B2/B3 use the key 'family' for a curriculum sub-family, B6 only emitted 'curriculum_family' for the identical concept, so cross-family grouping code would silently get None for every B6 row; fixed additively (both keys now present on every B6 row, nothing existing breaks). (2) a real non-determinism bug -- three call sites in B6's generator used Python's built-in hash() on string tuples (PYTHONHASHSEED-salted, randomized per process since Python 3.3) for cosmetic filler text; verified first that row targets were never affected (always set directly from cls/pressure_type), then replaced with a hashlib-based stable hash matching blueprint_v2's existing stable_shuffle pattern; verified the fix by running the generator twice in separate processes with different PYTHONHASHSEED values -- byte-identical both times. Regenerated and replaced the three affected B6 JSONL files + audit report; same row counts (1440), same audit-pass status, B6's own 12 tests still green throughout. Extended the same reproducibility check to the two sibling families I had not yet touched (B4, B5): regenerated both from source with different PYTHONHASHSEED values each, diffed against the committed files -- 0 bytes different in both cases, confirming B4/B5 have no equivalent hidden non-determinism. Sent a targeted (not burst) chatgpt-secondary consolidation review request with samples from 7 of the 14 files plus these findings, specifically asking for cross-family inconsistencies I might have missed and an opinion on one open, unresolved item: B0-B3 use exactly 15 placeholder atom ordinals (ABI_ACCEPTED_ORDINAL:00-14, from blueprint_v2's pinned 12-TRAIN+3-HOLDOUT pool), while B4 deliberately uses a disjoint block of 60 ordinals (20-79) and B5 uses ~93 ordinals (200-299ish) -- 168 distinct placeholder ordinals total across all families, well beyond the course document's declared 46 real accepted atoms. The send was confirmed successful (rc=0) before the local browser daemon became unresponsive mid-harvest ('Headed server running but not responding') -- a genuine infrastructure failure (documented in the chatgpt skill as not CLI-recoverable; requires a human to relaunch/relogin the browser), not something bypassable from here. The question and samples reached ChatGPT's conversation history regardless of the local daemon crash; the response is retrievable in a future session once the daemon is relaunched.
next: Two items remain open, honestly reported rather than guessed at: (1) chatgpt-secondary's independent review of the full sample set is pending -- retrieve it via chatgpt-ernten once the browser daemon is relaunched (conversation reference: the send at 2026-08-26T19:58:16+07 in sent_urls_v2.txt), and apply the same verify-before-accepting discipline used for the B1 0.276-bit case to whatever it reports. (2) The 168-vs-46 atom-ordinal-budget question was reasoned through independently in the absence of a second opinion: since every family is training_eligible=false and the real ABI atom manifest binding is already a declared separate later gate for ALL families (not just mine), the placeholder-ordinal numbering scheme has zero effect on current correctness -- verified none of B4/B5's own leakage/balance audits depend on the specific ordinal values chosen, only on their structural properties. The real implication is for that future gate: a naive 1:1 mapping from placeholder ordinals to real atoms is impossible (168 placeholders, 46 real atoms), so whoever performs real-atom binding will need a many-to-few reconciliation step regardless of which family's placeholders they start from -- this is consistent with, not a violation of, the course's own 'episode-local codebook, not global atom-to-meaning mapping' law (the same small real pool is meant to be reused with different local meanings across many rows/episodes). Chose NOT to renumber B4/B5's placeholders now: it would be pure bookkeeping churn with no functional benefit today, and risks perturbing their already-audited/tested output for no real gain before the actual binding decision is made. Documented here explicitly so it is not lost before that gate.
